issues.reason: Measures & units licenses ParticleFromNormal only for the symmetric hedges 'about / around / roughly / approximately'; 'nearly 4' entails a value below 4, so a normal centred on 4 asserts probability mass above 4 that the text excludes.

The Measure contract puts a magnitude on a dimension OF the named entity: 'point' is a unit, not a dimension, and the pull-back event has no 4-point value — what is 4 points is the change in the index — so the atom is both ill-typed and false as the vocabulary reads it.

This mistakes the reviewer's own gap 2 for a parse defect: no licensed relation ties a resulting measure to the event that produced it, while the emitted atom (Past (Measure standard_poors_500 point 1066.62 point)) is true of the sentence — the index stood at 1,066.62.

gaps_confirmed: a measured EXTENT OF CHANGE on an event ('pulled back by nearly 4 points') — Measure's contract is a dimension of an entity, MoreBy is a two-entity comparative, and no head records the size of a rise or fall
the ENDPOINT value reached by a change ('to 1,066.62') — no licensed relation ties a resulting measure to the event that produced it
one-sided approximators ('nearly / almost / just over / up to N') — only symmetric-sigma hedges are defined
index points as a unit with no underlying dimension noun — the scale slot has nothing to take
new_gaps: a Measure on an EVENT at all: only (Measure e duration <n> <unit>) is ever shown, and the instruction set never says whether any other event-level measure is well-formed
repair_summary: Removed (Measure sk_pull_back_1 point (ParticleFromNormal 4 0.4) point); with no licensed carrier for an extent of change the offending atom is dropped rather than re-encoded (gap recorded), and every other line is unchanged.
notes: The surviving endpoint atom keeps the unit duplicated into the scale slot, which is accepted as gap-territory improvisation under the calibration line — its entity really is the index and its value really is 1,066.62 points, so nothing false remains.
